records.quote: Putting the algebraic fraction in the simplest form is called reducing the algebraic fraction.
records.claim: Putting the algebraic fraction in the simplest form is called reducing the algebraic fraction.

records.quote: It is said that the algebraic fraction is in its simplest form
records.claim: An algebraic fraction is in its simplest form if there are no common factors between its numerator and denominator.

records.label: Example

records.stem: If $n(x)=\frac{x^3+x^2-6x}{x^4-13x^2+36}$ then reduce n(x) in the simplest form showing the domain of n.
solution: $n(x)=\frac{x}{(x+2)(x-3)}$ then cancel $(x+3)$, $(x-2)$ from the numerator and denominator.

records.quote: and the domain of n1 = R - {-3 , 3}
records.text: (1) $n_1(x)=\frac{x+3}{(x+3)(x-3)}=\frac{1}{x-3}$ and the domain of $n_1=R-\{-3,3\}$; $n_2(x)=\frac{2}{2(x-3)}=\frac{1}{x-3}$ and the domain of $n_2=R-\{-3\}$. i.e.: $n_1$ and $n_2$ are reduced to the same fraction but the domain of $n_1\neq$ the domain $n_2$

records.quote: and the domain of n1 = R - {-2}

records.quote: It is said that the two algebraic fractions n1 and n2 are equal
records.claim: Two algebraic fractions n1 and n2 are equal (n1 = n2) if two conditions are satisfied: the domain of n1 = the domain of n2, and n1(x) = n2(x) for each x in the common domain.
records.formula: $n_1 = n_2 \iff \text{domain of } n_1 = \text{domain of } n_2,\ n_1(x)=n_2(x)\ \forall x\in\text{common domain}$

records.label: Example
records.quote: If n1(x) = x^2/(x^3 - x^2) , n2(x) = (x^3 + x^2 + x)/(x^4 - x) prove that : n1 = n2
solution: from (1) and (2): since the domain of $n_1$ = the domain of $n_2$, $n_1(x)=n_2(x)$ for each $x\in\mathbb{R}-\{0,1\}$
